claude.sample_unit: deployed AI systems (1,814,000 inference events total)

links.outcome: Post-deployment discrimination and calibration versus validation-era performance
links.effect: System A AUROC 0.82 to 0.78, calibration slope 1.01 to 0.71 (mature); System B slope 0.99 to 0.69; System D AUROC 0.86 to 0.79, despite unchanged models.
links.quote: Across systems, post-deployment performance diverged from validation-era estimates despite unchanged model parameters, feature definitions, decision thresholds, and intended use.

links.outcome: Change in calibration slope and AUROC from validation to early deployment
links.effect: Mean Δ calibration slope -0.08 (3 mo), -0.11 (6 mo), -0.14 (9 mo); mean Δ AUROC -0.01 to -0.03.
links.quote: Calibration slope declined under each definition, with confidence intervals excluding zero, whereas AUROC differences were smaller and closer to zero.

links.outcome: Association and temporal precedence of input missingness/latency with calibration degradation
links.effect: Missingness βstd -0.42 to -0.21 across systems; negative in 12/12 specifications; telemetry ΔR² 0.21–0.28 vs population 0.05–0.07; temporal ordering preserved in all leave-one-out analyses.
links.quote: Input missingness and data latency preserved negative associations with calibration slope in all tested specifications.

unlisted_practices: Monitoring calibration (slope/intercept) rather than only AUROC for early detection of post-deployment degradation
Label-independent telemetry-first monitoring when outcome labels are delayed

openai.sample_unit: inference events across four deployed AI systems
models_evaluated: System A: Early clinical deterioration risk prediction
System C: Laboratory and structured-EHR diagnostic decision support

links.outcome: Post-deployment calibration and discrimination deterioration relative to validation
links.effect: First 6 months: mean Δ calibration slope -0.11 (-0.14 to -0.08), versus mean Δ AUROC -0.02 (-0.03 to -0.01). Performance degradation occurred across all four systems.
links.quote: Across systems, post-deployment performance diverged from validation-era estimates despite unchanged model parameters, feature definitions, decision thresholds, and intended use.

links.outcome: Operational telemetry as an early indicator of calibration degradation
links.effect: Missingness βstd ranged from -0.46 to -0.31; latency from -0.39 to -0.24. Negative associations persisted in 12/12 specifications for each; telemetry preceded or co-evolved with calibration degradation.
links.quote: Workflow-associated telemetry signals, particularly missingness and latency, continued to precede or co-evolve with calibration degradation.

links.effect: validation-era performance deteriorated post-deployment across all 4 evaluated AI systems
links.quote: Across all systems, validation-era performance did not persist as a stable operational property after deployment.

links.effect: silent calibration failure emerged earlier and more consistently than discrimination loss
links.quote: Across systems, degradation often appeared first as calibration failure without comparable loss of discrimination.

links.outcome: effect of data missingness on calibration
links.effect: input missingness and data latency were strongly associated with declining calibration
links.quote: Input missingness and data latency were most strongly associated with declining calibration slope in Systems A and B.

unlisted_practices: monitoring label-independent operational telemetry like input missingness and data latency as early warning signals for model degradation

screen.practice: post-deployment drift monitoring with label-independent operational telemetry
screen.reason: Evaluates the effectiveness of different post-deployment monitoring practices (label-independent operational telemetry vs. outcome-based monitoring) across four deployed clinical AI systems.

primary.practice: post-deployment operational and calibration drift monitoring
